newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-ELS CRUSHES BROOKS, SINGH OUTLASTS LEHMAN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS CRUSHES BROOKS, SINGH OUTLASTS LEHMAN.

text.p: Ernie Els romped into the World Matchplay final with a near-record 10-8 victory over American Mark Brooks on Saturday and could become the first player to win three successive titles in the 33-year-old championship.

The South African won easily as Brooks struggled with his game on the soggy 6,957-yard West Course, and in Sunday'a final faces Vijay Singh of Fiji, who scored a dramatic 37th-hole win over British Open champion Tom Lehman.

Lehman three-putted from 90 feet at the par-five 36th as the unseeded Singh reached the final for the first time in four visits after he birdied the 36th to force a playoff and then birdied the first extra hole with a 12-foot putt.

Apart from a burst of three birdies in four holes to close out the morning round, Els made only one other birdie on the first 26 holes before he birdied the 27th from nine feet and the 28th with a 25-foot putt to close out the match.

Els said: "Mark made all the mistakes while I just kept plugging away, making my pars with birdies here and there. Nothing great, but good enough. Now I have to get my game into cruise control for the final."

The South African is the fifth player to seek the hat-trick of titles. Compatriot Gary Player won in 1965 and 1966, American Hale Irwin in 1974 and 1975 and Seve Ballesteros in 1981 and 1982, and 1984 and 1985.

Els's margin of victory was the joint second largest in the history of the event behind Tom Watson's 11 and 9 destruction of South African Dale Hayes in 1978 and level with Arnold Palmer's 10 and 8 win over Roberto de Vicenzo in 1966.
"I tried on every shot but the harder I tried, the worse it got," said Brooks, the U.S. PGA champion who could not stop from pushing his ball far to the right.
"I'm not embarrassed. I was more frustrated than anything," the 35-year-old Texan added. "Hitting to the right is not usually a problem for me. Usually if I have a problem it's hitting left."
"I even hit balls for 45 minutes between rounds, then hit an even worse shot off the tee at the 19th," he said.

Brooks, who beat Colin Montgomerie on Friday, did not win a hole against Els and reached the greens in regulation only nine times in 28 holes, all except the last two leaving him with impossibly long putts.

After the morning round, Els was already six shots ahead despite making only two birdies and, while he trailed by that margin against American Steve Stricker on Friday before winning at the last, a similar reversal was unlikely and so it proved.
Els won the 19th and 20th holes as Brooks bogeyed both and after seven successive halves in pars, the South African closed out the contest with his two final birdies.

Lehman praised Singh after their superb battle. "Vijay played extremely well. His second shot at the playoff hole was phenomenal. He made maybe one mistake. I made more birdies but I also had more bogeys.

"Three putts at the 36th, the ball was in my court. Vijay had the same putt this morning and was 10 feet short so I was surprised when I hit mine seven feet past. On the second putt I played it outside left, but it didn't move."
Singh has beaten U.S. money leader Phil Mickelson, U.S. Open champion Steve Jones and now the British Open champion this week.
"I did not make a bogey yesterday and I had only one today. I will try to do the same against Ernie, make him win the holes with birdies," Singh said.
"My second shot at the playoff came out of the rough just as I wanted it to. It was about 180 yards and I hit a five iron."
His 12-foot winning birdie almost stopped short, but just dropped in after Lehman had made a par.
